review.summary: SWE-bench contributes a substantial, realistic benchmark of issue-resolution tasks drawn from real GitHub repositories, framing code generation as repository-level engineering evaluated against tests. The reported baselines show difficulty for evaluated models, and the authors clearly identify Python-only coverage and test-based evaluation as scope limitations.

observations.claim: The benchmark grounds tasks in real GitHub issues and pull requests across multiple Python repositories.
observations.quote:
2,294 software engi-
neering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests
across 12 popular Python repositories.

observations.claim: The paper reports low performance on the benchmark even with oracle retrieval, supporting its claim that these tasks challenge the tested models.
observations.quote:
Claude 2 and GPT-4 solve a mere4.8% and 1.7% of instances re-
spectively, even when provided with an oracle retriever.

observations.claim: The current task collection covers only Python, so generalization to other languages and domains remains unestablished.
observations.quote:
SWE-bench task instances are all in Python; we hope to ap-
ply SWE-bench’s task instance collection procedure to expand its coverage to more programming languages and domains.

observations.claim: Execution-based tests alone do not guarantee that generated solutions are reliable.
observations.quote:
relying solely on this method is insufficient to guarantee reliable performance of
model generations

unresolved_questions: I did not inspect the benchmark-construction procedure or detailed experimental sections; how are issue/PR pairs filtered and test relevance validated, and how robust are headline results across model configurations?
How well does benchmark success correlate with expert judgments of correctness, maintainability, and usefulness in real engineering work?
